    Torsion pairs #

    • Definition 2.4: torsion pairs (IsTorsionPair).
    • Proposition 2.5: the torsion pairs are the pretorsion theories with T ∩ F = 0 (isTorsionPair_iff). When Z = 0, Z-trivial morphisms are the zero morphisms, and short Z-preexact sequences are short exact sequences.
    • Corollary 3.9: the torsion pairs form a complete sublattice of the pretorsion theories containing the least and greatest elements (IsTorsion.sInf, IsTorsion.sSup, isTorsion_bot, isTorsion_top), and a torsion pair is determined by, and ordered by, its first component (IsTorsion.le_iff).
    source
    def PretorsionImageClosed.Statement.IsTorsionPair {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [CategoryTheory.Abelian C] (T F : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty C) :
    Prop

    Definition 2.4. (T, F) is a torsion pair: there are no nonzero morphisms from T to F, and every object X sits in a short exact sequence 0 → T' → X → F' → 0 with T' ∈ T and F' ∈ F.

      theorem PretorsionImageClosed.Statement.isTorsionPair_iff {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [CategoryTheory.Abelian C] (T F : Subcategory C) :
      IsTorsionPair T.prop F.prop ↔ IsPretorsionTheory T.prop F.prop ∧ ∀ (X : C), (T.prop ⊓ F.prop) X → CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero X

      Proposition 2.5. (T, F) is a torsion pair iff it is a pretorsion theory with T ∩ F = 0.
